newsitem.title: USA: Utah sues tobacco companies to recoup Medicaid fees.
newsitem.headline: Utah sues tobacco companies to recoup Medicaid fees.

text.p: Utah, in a bid to recoup the cost of state Medicaid funds spent on tobacco-related disease, on Monday sued a group of tobacco companies, the state attorney general said.
Utah, which has the lowest rate of smokers in the United States, joined 15 other states and a number of cities and counties that have filed lawsuits against the tobacco giants.

Sued in federal court were tobacco giants Philip Morris Co. Inc, RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp's R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co., B.A.T Industries Plc's Brown & Williamson Tobacco Corp. and Brooke Group Ltd's Liggett Group Inc.'s Liggett & Meyers.
"We sued to recoup Medicaid costs, but also to put a hold on the targetting of youth," said Todd Utzinger, a spokesman for Utah Attorney General Jan Graham.
"At least one-third of those kids hooked on cigarettes will die as a result, and that is why I have filed suit against the giant cigarette makers," Graham said in a statement.
While the state did not specify a dollar figure in its lawsuit, Utzinger said that tobacco-related costs to Medicaid in Utah from 1993 until the present stood at $128 million.
Michael York, spokesman for Philip Morris, said he had not seen the lawsuit but believed it would be a "copycat, cookie cutter lawsuit" based on earlier state cases.
"So far we not seen any cases with any legal merit and we don't expect to," York said.
In May 1994 Mississippi become the first state to sue the industry to recoup Medicaid costs of smokers, but other states, including Minnesota and Florid have also filed lawsuits.

Smoking rates in Utah are the lowest in the nation, due in a great part to the influence of the Mormon Church, said Wayne Davis, Executive Director of the American Lung Society of Utah. Some 15.6 percent of Utah residents smoke, compared with about 25 percent for the rest of the country. The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints prohibits smoking.
